en: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great community of monks and a great host of bodhisattvas.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya, who was seated in that assembly of gods, rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the ripening of this gift of Dharma?
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya:

And whoever, Maitreya, were to fill trichiliocosm world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges with the seven precious jewels and give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones; and whoever, out of compassion, were to establish even a single verse within the mental continuum of another—Maitreya, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this latter mass of merit.

It does not bear comparison even to a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth (koṭī) part, nor a hundred-ten-millionth part, nor a thousand-ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand-ten-millionth part; it does not admit of any number, fraction, calculation, or analogy.
The Blessed One said this. Having spoken thus, the Sugata, the Teacher, then further said this:

"Whoever here, with a joyful and virtuous mind, should give to the Jinas world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, filled with jewels; and whoever should teach even a single verse to a single sentient being—[the latter’s merit is greater]. [1]

That vast gift of jewels does not attain even a fraction, nor any number, of the gift of verses acquired through compassion; what need is there to mention two or three? Thus spoke the Blessed One. With joyful minds, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, those other Bodhisattvas, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Great Vehicle Sūtra entitled "The Questions of the Noble Maitreya," the sixteenth, is completed.
